title: Waste hierarchy and segregation (India)
summary: Prefer prevention and reuse, then recycling of segregated dry waste, then responsible disposal. Follow your Urban Local Body's published segregation rules. EcoPath.AI does not invent GHMC ward schedules or recyclers.
content:
The Central Pollution Control Board publishes national guidance and rules related to waste. Cities implement segregation (typically wet/dry, sometimes domestic hazardous) differently.

Practical household order:
1. Prevent — do not buy what will be thrown immediately.
2. Reuse — jars, bags, containers you will actually use.
3. Recycle — only materials your local collection actually accepts.
4. Dispose — residual waste as directed locally.

E-waste and batteries should not go in mixed household waste. Use authorised e-waste channels listed by your state board or producer — look up the current list; this article does not name shops.

Mark this article's local operational details as unverified until you confirm your ULB circular.
applicability_conditions: Generates household or institutional waste in India
implementation_steps: Keep wet and dry waste separate if your ULB requires it
Confirm accepted dry-waste types from an official local notice
Log estimated kg of residual waste monthly if you want a baseline
Use Circular Living in EcoPath.AI for item-level questions, then confirm locally
